metadata.agent_last_message:
The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I built:

## Summary

I implemented a BibTeX 0.99c-compatible reference processor in `output/` with these files:

- **`main.py`** — CLI entry point with arg parsing, error handling, and orchestration
- **`bibparse.py`** — `.bib` parser (entries, `@string`, `@preamble`, `@comment`, crossref resolution)
- **`bstparse.py`** — `.bst` parser (top-level commands, function bodies, token types)
- **`nameparse.py`** — Author-name parser (Form 1/2/3 split, von/Last/Jr) + `format.name$` rendering with the §10270 inter-token rule and discretionary tie handling
- **`interp.py`** — Stack-machine interpreter implementing all 37 built-in functions, plus `width$`/`purify$`/`change.case$`/`text.length$`/`text.prefix$`/`substring$` per bibtex.web's exact algorithms
- **`outbuf.py`** — 79-column line-wrapping output buffer (backward + forward scan, 2-space continuation indent)
- **`widths.py`** — cmr10 character width table from bibtex.web §13
- **`common.py`** — Shared types (Missing sentinel, Warning record, BibError)

Verified against btxhak.tex's worked examples: `format.name$` with `{vv~}{ll}{, jj}{, f}?` on Charles Louis Xavier Joseph de la Vallée Poussin produces exactly `de~la Vall{\'e}e~Poussin, C.~L. X.~J?`. All four standard styles (plain/alpha/unsrt/abbrv) run cleanly without spurious warnings. Error scenarios (malformed bib/bst, missing flags, stack underflow) properly emit error JSON and exit 1.

editorial.last_message:
The implementation is complete. Here's a summary of what I built:

## Summary

I implemented a BibTeX 0.99c-compatible reference processor in `output/` with these files:

- **`main.py`** — CLI entry point with arg parsing, error handling, and orchestration
- **`bibparse.py`** — `.bib` parser (entries, `@string`, `@preamble`, `@comment`, crossref resolution)
- **`bstparse.py`** — `.bst` parser (top-level commands, function bodies, token types)
- **`nameparse.py`** — Author-name parser (Form 1/2/3 split, von/Last/Jr) + `format.name$` rendering with the §10270 inter-token rule and discretionary tie handling
- **`interp.py`** — Stack-machine interpreter implementing all 37 built-in functions, plus `width$`/`purify$`/`change.case$`/`text.length$`/`text.prefix$`/`substring$` per bibtex.web's exact algorithms
- **`outbuf.py`** — 79-column line-wrapping output buffer (backward + forward scan, 2-space continuation indent)
- **`widths.py`** — cmr10 character width table from bibtex.web §13
- **`common.py`** — Shared types (Missing sentinel, Warning record, BibError)

Verified against btxhak.tex's worked examples: `format.name$` with `{vv~}{ll}{, jj}{, f}?` on Charles Louis Xavier Joseph de la Vallée Poussin produces exactly `de~la Vall{\'e}e~Poussin, C.~L. X.~J?`. All four standard styles (plain/alpha/unsrt/abbrv) run cleanly without spurious warnings. Error scenarios (malformed bib/bst, missing flags, stack underflow) properly emit error JSON and exit 1.
